blocks.text: The peacock, proud of its many-coloured feathers, etc. And among the Grammarians, who hold that ταὼν [taōn] is so called ἀπὸ τῆς τάσεως [apo tēs taseōs], from extension, or παρὰ τὸ τείνειν τὴν οὐράν· τὸ γὰρ ζῶον ἐναβρυνόμενον τῷ ἑαυτοῦ κάλλει τοῖς ὁρῶσι τὴν οὐρὰν ἑξαπλοῦν ἀποδεικνύει [para to teinein tēn ouran; to gar zōon enabrynomenon tō heautou kallei tois horōsi tēn ouran hexaploun apodeiknyei], because it spreads out its tail; for this animal, proud of its beauty, displays its sixfold tail to the onlookers. And in Damir too the Arabs say that it is in its nature حب الزهو بنفسه والخيلا والاعجاب بريشه وعقد ذنبه كالطاقة اذا كانت الانثي ناظرة اليه [ḥubb al-zahw bi-nafsihi wa-l-khuyalāʾ wa-l-iʿjāb bi-rīshihi wa-ʿaqd dhanabihi ka-l-ṭāqa idhā kānat al-unthá nāẓiratan ilayhi] that it loves to gaze upon itself with vainglory and pride, and admires its feathers, and arranges its tail into a circle when the female looks at it.
